item.text: {"text":"Recent research supports text as complementary item information, but provides limited direct evidence for a lightweight, from-scratch text encoder inside NextItNet. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines textual item representations with sequential modeling and reports content ablations; however, it uses BERT, a SASRec-derived backbone, and reviews, with reviews contributing most. Its gains therefore do not establish that titles/descriptions alone will improve this constrained setting. [DWSRec (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) shows that the geometry of pretrained text embeddings affects recommendation quality, reinforcing that semantic similarity requires adaptation to recommendation objectives.\n\nA constraint-compatible hypothesis is to retain [NextItNet’s dilated convolutional residual backbone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), adding randomly initialized token embeddings with masked mean pooling or a small text CNN over titles/descriptions. Project and gate these features into item-ID embeddings; jointly train the entire network using next-item supervision and use the same item representation for candidate scoring. This is a proposed adaptation, not a verified result from the retrieved papers. Preserve item-specific ID capacity so shared wording does not collapse distinct products. Compare ID-only, title-only augmentation, and title-plus-description augmentation through separate single-model trials using macro validation HR@10; retain one checkpoint per category. Text can expose explicit distinctions such as edition, format, dimensions, or model identifiers when present, but cannot establish purchase purpose, actual compatibility, or satisfied needs."}
